question: Resolve Schedule I remittance/lockbox addresses to recipients' program locations for the top-50 sponsors FY2023-2024: flag non-ZCTA lockbox ZIPs (e.g. 50037 Boone IA, 45277 Cincinnati OH, 32862 Orlando FL), compare with each recipient's EO BMF and latest 990 header address, and restate state and metro shares on an office-address basis
conclusion_affected: Whether IA/OH/FL dollars and the Schedule I vs BMF state disagreement (5.6% of EIN-matched dollars) change state rankings or per-capita outliers
rationale: IA receives $644m on the Schedule I address basis but $231m on the BMF-state basis; 10.3% of dollars carry ZIPs that are not ZCTAs (PO boxes and lockboxes)

question: Extend the community-foundation local-share measure beyond the 22 top-50 CFs: compute own-state and own-metro shares of Schedule I dollars for the 100 largest community foundations (CY2022-2024 e-file returns), split DAF vs discretionary grants where Schedule I purpose text or Part IX allows, and test whether local share falls with DAF share of grants
conclusion_affected: Whether 'community foundations keep money local' holds outside the largest CFs and whether DAF-heavy CFs (SVCF 69% own-state but 4% own-metro; Chicago Community Trust 20%) behave like national sponsors
rationale: Top-50 CFs: pooled own-state share 60% (median 71%, range 20-92%) vs national sponsors 8% (median 5%)

question: Add Schedule F (grants to foreign organisations and individuals, Part I by region) for the top-50 sponsors FY2023-2024 so that the geography covers foreign grants, and reconcile with NTEE Q domestic intermediaries (e.g. MSF USA, World Central Kitchen) that re-grant abroad
conclusion_affected: Size of the international slice that Schedule I Part II cannot see (foreign-address Part II lines are only $0.3m)
rationale: Schedule I Part II covers domestic organisations only; international is understated in both the sector and geography outputs
